questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Resources: Human and Non-Human' refers to.
questions.a: A resource is anything usable to satisfy a need. Resources divide into human -- time, energy, knowledge, skills -- and non-human -- money, goods, community facilities and natural materials; each again may be individual or shared. Values and habits decide whether these are used or squandered.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Resources: Human and Non-Human'.
questions.a: Time, energy, money and skills are all one currency -- resources -- and management is spending them wisely.

concepts.title: Management Process: Planning, Organising, Implementing, Controlling

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Management Process: Planning, Organising, Implementing, Controlling' refers to.
questions.a: Management is the decision process that turns resources into goals: planning what to do, organising means and tasks, implementing the plan, and controlling by judging results against the standard. The loop feeds back -- judged outcomes revise the next plan.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Management Process: Planning, Organising, Implementing, Controlling'.
questions.a: Plan, organise, act, check -- the four-beat rhythm that converts resources into achieved goals.

concepts.title: Time and Energy Management; Work Simplification

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Time and Energy Management; Work Simplification' refers to.
questions.a: Time and energy are the human resources that technique can stretch: schedules and to-do lists discipline time, while work simplification -- better sequence, fewer motions, right tools, combining tasks -- saves energy. Rest and posture conserve the worker as much as the work.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Time and Energy Management; Work Simplification'.
questions.a: Schedule the hours, simplify the motions -- stretch the two resources that cannot be bought.
